seo.title: About
seo.description: Dr. Lauretta Ogbum came into psychotherapy from risk assessment in the energy sector. Twenty-five years married, PhD in Psychology, and an assessor's discipline applied to relationships.

hero.eyebrow: From risk assessment to the human heart
hero.title: I did not begin in psychology.
paragraphs:
I'm a psychotherapist, counsellor and coach. I work with people who are carrying something, anxiety, grief, burnout, a marriage that's gone quiet, a version of themselves they don't recognise anymore.

Most of them are managing. That's usually the problem. They're functioning well enough that nobody's asked how they are in a long time.

How I got here.
I didn't start in psychology. Most of my working life has been in security and risk, and I'm still in it. It's not a past career I left behind for something more meaningful. I do both.

People find that combination odd until they think about it. Security work puts you around people on their worst days: after the incident, during the emergency, in the hours when things have gone wrong and someone has to stay calm. I spent years doing that before I ever sat in a therapy room.

What I kept noticing was how many people were handling enormous things without any support at all. Not because help didn't exist, but because asking felt like admitting something. So I went and trained properly and built a practice alongside the work I was already doing.


I've been doing both ever since. The security work keeps me around real pressure. The practice is where I do something about it.

'm fairly direct. Not harsh, but I'm not going to spend six sessions circling something we both know is the issue. If you want someone who will only agree with you, I'm probably not it.

I don't take sides in couples work. I'll say that early and I'll mean it, because most people arrive half-expecting me to declare a winner. Nobody wins in my room. That's rather the point.

I'm not easily shocked. Twenty-odd years around security work and a decade in practice takes care of that. You can say the thing you've been rehearsing.

And I won't pretend it's quick. Some things resolve in six sessions. Some take a year. I'll tell you honestly which one I think you're looking at, and I'd rather lose the booking than promise you a timeline I can't deliver.
What I work with
Anxiety and stress. Depression and low mood. Grief, bereavement, miscarriage, divorce, the losses people don't think count. Trauma. Burnout. Self-worth. Life transitions, including the ones that look good on paper and still feel like grief.

And relationships: couples, engaged couples, people who aren't sure whether to stay, people who aren't sure whether to start. It's the area I'm best known for and it's where I've done most of my writing — but it isn't the only room I work in.

beliefs.title: Four things I will say out loud
beliefs.intro: These are not marketing lines. They are the assumptions everything in my practice is built on, and it is fair for you to know them before you book anything.

notForYou.title: When I am not the right person
notForYou.intro: I would rather tell you this now than take a booking and disappoint you at session three. If any of the following is what you are looking for, I am not it — and in the free conversation I will say so and point you somewhere better.
items: You want someone to confirm that your partner is the problem.
You want a verdict on whether to stay or go, delivered by me.
You want it fixed in three sessions because twenty years is inconvenient.
You want a diagnosis of somebody who is not in the room.

closing.intro: Which does not make me an authority on your marriage. It does mean I have made most of the ordinary mistakes personally, before I ever saw them professionally.
